questions.question: Which skip-gram pairs does skipgram_pairs(["a", "b", "c"], window=1) emit?
options: (a,c), (c,a) only
Every ordered pair, including tokens more than one position away
questions.explanation: The loop visits neighbors within one position and skips i==j, producing the four adjacent ordered pairs.

questions.question: What shapes do init_embeddings(vocab_size=5, dim=16, ...) return?
options: W is (16,5) and W_prime is (5,1)
W and W_prime are both (5,16)
Both arrays are (5,5)
One scalar vector is returned for the entire vocabulary
questions.explanation: There is one 16-dimensional row for each vocabulary item in each of the two embedding tables.

questions.question: Which IDs does train exclude while sampling negative contexts for a center/context pair?
options: Only the first vocabulary ID
Every ID that appears in the document
The positive context ID and the center ID
No IDs; negatives may equal the positive context
questions.explanation: The candidate filter keeps n only when it differs from both ctx_idx and c_idx.

questions.question: What is the positive-pair error term in train_pair?
options: sigmoid(v_c @ u_pos) + 1
v_c - u_pos, without a sigmoid
The cosine distance between every vocabulary row
sigmoid(v_c @ u_pos) - 1
questions.explanation: A positive pair targets probability one, so the logistic error is sigmoid(score)-1 before the gradient update.

questions.question: What similarity does nearest use when ranking candidate words?
options: Cosine similarity after normalizing each row and the target vector
Raw Euclidean distance without normalization
The number of characters shared by two words
The order in which the words entered the vocabulary
questions.explanation: nearest builds W_norm and a normalized target, then sorts W_norm @ target in descending order.

questions.question: What information does skip-gram add that a bag-of-words vector lacks?
options: It preserves exact document order in a sparse count matrix
It trains vectors from local context, so words with similar neighborhoods can become nearby
It guarantees that every synonym receives an identical vector
It removes the need for a vocabulary or negative samples
questions.explanation: The center/context objective uses neighboring words as a learning signal; it does not store the original sequence verbatim.
